scenes.headline: How an agent checks its own speed-ups
scenes.sub: A benchmark loop under a WebGPU renderer
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Metronome! A coding agent made a WebGPU renderer much faster. The interesting part is how it knew each change helped.

scenes.text: Time CPU and GPU apart, and call a change faster only when it is real and big.
scenes.say: The idea: time the CPU and the GPU separately, and call a change faster only when it is both real and big.

steps.say: The agent writes a change to the renderer.
The harness warms up until shaders stop compiling, then times many frames.
Each fresh process gives one number, its median.
Two gates decide: keep the change, or drop it and try the next idea.

scenes.title: One frame, two clocks
scenes.text: frame cost = max(CPU p95, GPU p95)

parts.say: The CPU side is JavaScript building command buffers.
The GPU side comes from timestamp queries slipped into every render pass.
Frame cost is whichever side is slower.

scenes.title: The two gates
scenes.say: A change must clear two gates.

items.say: First, a rank test asks whether the difference is real.
Second, the median shift must be at least five percent, or the verdict is neutral.
And the work must still be done. A frame that drew nothing fails.

left.title: String key
left.say: One public fix: bind groups were looked up by a string built from every resource id.

right.title: XOR key
right.say: Now the key is two numbers combined with exclusive or, so swapping one texture costs almost nothing.

steps.say: The launch video says five point nine times faster across twenty seven scenes.

steps.note: the method, in tiny grey type
steps.say: The fine print: a geometric mean of frame cost, one laptop, one browser.

scenes.label: 860 bind-group lookups per frame, down from 71 µs
scenes.note: PixiJS pull request 12278, the author's numbers
scenes.say: The public fixes save microseconds a frame. The big multiple lives in code we can't read.

scenes.text: An agent can only find real speed-ups when the benchmark refuses noise, tiny wins and empty frames.
scenes.mark: refuses noise, tiny wins and empty frames
scenes.say: So: an agent finds real speed-ups only when its benchmark refuses noise, tiny wins and empty frames.

recap: Judge block medians with two gates
scenes.say: Time both clocks. Judge with two gates. Prove the work was done.
